question.text: Which of the following securities CANNOT be held in dematerialised form?

explanation.text: The Logic: Eligible securities for dematerialisation listed in the source include shares, scrips, stocks, bonds, debentures, IDRs, Electronic Gold Receipts, mutual fund units, rights under CIS, VCF, CDs, commercial paper, money market instruments, government securities, and unlisted securities. Post Office savings certificates are not included in this list of eligible securities. The Trap: Candidates may think only equity shares can be dematerialised. The eligible-securities list is much wider — Electronic Gold Receipts, mutual fund units, and commercial paper are all eligible. Note: When deciding what can be held in demat form, refer to the eligible-securities list — Post Office savings certificates do not appear in it.
